explanation: Further heating converts mercuric oxide into liquid metallic mercury and oxygen gas — the second step in extracting mercury from cinnabar, and historically one of the reactions used in discovering oxygen itself.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: A reddish solid residue of mercuric oxide.

thermal.visual_cue: Needs strong, sustained heating to decompose.

beaker_view.observation: Heated further, the reddish oxide decomposes into silvery droplets of liquid mercury, with oxygen gas escaping.
